title: Photovoltaic Response of Perovskite Solar Cells Using a Ternary Organic BHJ as Electron Transport Layer: A Device Simulation Approach
content: The efficiency of formamidinium lead iodide (FAPbI₃) solar cells is restricted by re-combination at the electron-transport interface and the limited processing window of traditional electron transport layers. Using a ternary organic bulk heterojunction (BHJ) instead of the oxide electron-transport layer, we propose and numerically analyze an ZnO/D18:Y6:PCBM/FAPbI₃/Spiro-OMeTAD device.  SCAPS-1D (AM1.5G, 300 K) sim-ulations were calibrated against an experimental ITO/ZnO/SnO₂/FAPbI₃/Spiro-OMeTAD/Ag device (21.91% PCE), with 5.4% open-circuit voltage and 4.1% power-conversion efficiency errors. We next optimized the hole-transport layer, ZnO buffer, BHJ ETL, and absorber sequentially and assessed quantum efficiency, temperature dependency, and ETL trap tolerance. The optimized cell achieves a PCE of 24.35% (Voc = 1.14 V, Jsc = 26.54 mA cm⁻², FF = 80.4%) using a 700 nm absorber thickness. ETL doping at 1020 cm⁻³ increases open-circuit voltage to 1.16 V and FF to 85.3% via reducing series resistance and interfacial recombination. Quantum efficiency surpasses 98% at 300–550 nm. Performance decreases at increas-ing temperatures due to open-circuit voltage and FF losses, and when the electron transport layer's trap density increases from 10¹¹ to 10¹⁸ cm⁻³ (Voc 1.151 to 1.083 V). Results provide quantifiable design objectives for experimental organic-BHJ/perovskite hybrid cells.
